summary: enuma-elish is not tagged cosmogony: the corpus's paradigmatic creation epic has no origin-events tag, and its best concept match is theurgy (-4.84)

analysis.author: Hermes Agent
analysis.content:
Found while investigating why enuma-elish emits zero derived PARALLELS (todo:9097deed; full record in docs/summary/derived-parallels-cutover-2026-08-14.md).

THE GAP. concept.cosmogony exists in the taxonomy (cosmology.origin_events, alongside letters_of_creation, tzimtzum, fall_of_sophia, frashokereti, apocatastasis) and is applied across the corpus: 123 EXPRESSES tags over 20 texts in 10 traditions (celtic, christian_mysticism, finnic, gnosticism, hinduism, native_american, norse, shinto, western_esoteric, zoroastrianism). The Enuma Elish -- the paradigmatic ancient Near Eastern creation epic, and arguably the single most cosmogonic text in the corpus -- carries none of it. Nor any other origin_events concept.

It was never even proposed. staged_tags for mesopotamian.enuma-elish.* contains no row whose concept_id matches cosmogon% in any status. This is not a proposal that review rejected; the tagger never suggested it.

WHAT IT IS TAGGED WITH INSTEAD, and the tier story. 12 chunks, 76 live EXPRESSES: living_god (12), anthropomorphism (11), cosmic_dualism (10), sacred_names (12 across both tiers), divine_providence (6), logos (3), covenant (3), plus ritual_purity, numerical_mysticism, prayer, theurgy. Domain breakdown: almost entirely theology.* and praxis.*, with logos the lone cosmology.* entry -- and that is cosmology.divine_structure, not origin_events. A Babylonian theomachy is being described as covenant, prayer and theurgy.

Tier split is 48 proposed / 28 verified. The staged_tags queue still holds 49 pending rows for this text, so most of what is live was written by scripts/auto_promote.py at tier='proposed' without per-row human review, and the review queue for it was never worked. Tagging model was the 27B teacher (Qwen3.5-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf), not the 4B fine-tune -- so this is not the off-distribution 4B failure mode from todo:667f1aaf, and the node-10 routing standard is not implicated.

HOW IT SURFACED, AND WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE BEFORE. The derived-parallels generator scores (concept definition, chunk body) with the thin scorer and needs a partner clearing config[scoring].min_grade = -4.415. Every one of enuma-elish's 76 pairs falls below that; its BEST match is concept.theurgy at -4.84, and the scorer is right to say a creation narrative is not about theurgy. Zero pairs clear, so zero edges.

Pass C never consulted concepts at all -- it proposed pairs by vector adjacency and had an LLM classify them -- so it happily produced 249 PARALLELS for this text on top of tags that do not describe it. The cutover did not break enuma-elish; it is the first mechanism that ever made edge production depend on tag quality, and this text failed that dependency immediately.

CAUTION ON THE OBVIOUS FIX. Do NOT reach for lowering min_grade or rank-based selection to "restore" this work's edges. For works whose tags are right but whose scores are low (see the cutover doc: lesser-holy-assembly tops at sephirot, yasna-43 at ritual_fire, bhagavad-gita-chapter-02 at meditation, diamond-sutra at sunyata_emptiness, tao-te-ching at wu_wei) rank-based selection is safe and correct. Here it is actively harmful: it would manufacture panels annotated "Shared concept: Theurgy. (derived)" on the Enuma Elish, which is worse than an empty strip. This work needs re-tagging, not a threshold change.

SUGGESTED WORK. Re-run node 10 over mesopotamian.enuma-elish with the 27B and the current taxonomy, specifically checking whether origin_events concepts are reachable for it; work the 49 pending staged_tags rows; then re-derive. Worth checking descent-of-inanna at the same time (35 pairs, best -5.21, top concept funerary_navigation) since it is the other mesopotamian text on the weak list and may share the cause.

analysis.author: Hermes Agent
analysis.content:
CORRECTION (2026-08-15). This ticket says the Enuma Elish is mis-tagged and implies the 27B failed to propose the obvious concept for a creation epic. That is wrong, and the real cause is systemic rather than specific to this text.

THE DATES. concept.cosmogony was added to concepts/taxonomy.toml on 2026-06-06 (commit 23591e03, "concepts: add animism, cosmogony, world_tree_axis, word_power_incantation, ancestor_veneration, shapeshifting_transformation"). The Enuma Elish's staged_tags were produced under prompt_version v1 and reviewed on 2026-05-11 -- twenty-six days EARLIER. The tagger never proposed cosmogony because the concept did not exist when the text was tagged. There is no judgment failure here to fix.

That also explains the distribution that looked so damning: cosmogony carries 123 tags over 20 texts in 10 traditions, all of which were tagged after 2026-06-06. Mesopotamian was tagged in May, so it is not among them. The concept looks widely adopted and the one obvious text looks skipped, purely as an artifact of when each was processed.

THIS IS TAXONOMY DRIFT, AND IT IS NOT SMALL. Nothing re-tags existing works when the taxonomy grows, so every work carries the concept vocabulary of whenever it happened to be tagged. Taxonomy additions since the bulk tagging began:
    2026-05-02  a59d32ad  expand taxonomy (Tertium Organum / Heroic Enthusiasts)
    2026-05-15  a454573a  add 10 concepts surfaced by Phase 1 new sources
    2026-06-06  23591e03  add 6 (animism, cosmogony, world_tree_axis, word_power_incantation, ancestor_veneration, shapeshifting_transformation)
    2026-06-07  b333ac95  add shamanic_journey
    2026-07-16  e649882a  add astral_light, magical_equilibrium, magical_will
Tags by review month: 2026-04 = 130, 2026-05 = 18,086, 2026-06 = 15,238, 2026-07 = 13,250, 2026-08 = 9,044. So roughly 18,200 tags from April and May were produced blind to at least the ten concepts introduced from 2026-06-06 onward, and a further slice of May predates the 2026-05-15 addition of ten more.

The affected works are not randomly distributed either. The June 6 batch is heavy with animist, cosmogonic and world-axis concepts -- exactly the vocabulary that oral, mythological and indigenous traditions need -- while the traditions most likely to have been tagged early are the ones that entered the corpus first.

WHAT THE FIX ACTUALLY IS. Not "re-tag the Enuma Elish". A scoped taxonomy-backfill pass: for each work, determine the concepts that did not exist at its tagging date, and re-run node 10 restricted to that delta, asking only "does this chunk express any of these newer concepts?" That is far cheaper than full re-tagging and it lands in node 11's queue like any other proposal, with the owner's apply gate intact. The Enuma Elish is the exemplar, not the scope.

CONSEQUENCE FOR todo:7427712c (the selection-frame plan). Its acceptance test was "a correct threshold fix leaves the Enuma Elish empty", justified by this ticket's mis-tagging claim. That premise is now false: once the backfill gives the text cosmogony, it should legitimately earn panels on its own merits, and a fix that keeps it empty would be wrong. The acceptance test must be restated as "a work whose tags are genuinely inapt produces no panels", exercised by a fixture rather than by this text.

It also argues for ordering: calibrating a selection rule against a corpus with known-stale tags means calibrating on data we already know is wrong for ~18k tags. The backfill should run, or at least be measured, before the threshold operating point is fixed.
